summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back and nausea, consistent with an acute flare. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, analgesia, and antiemetics. Her course was complicated by aspiration pneumonia, diagnosed on chest X-ray, and treated with a six-day course of levofloxacin and metronidazole. Due to persistent pain with oral intake, TPN was initiated via a left basilic vein PICC line placed on hospital day 6. Her symptoms improved with TPN, and she was discharged home with ongoing TPN, strict NPO status aside from sips and medications, and plans for outpatient follow-up with GI and PCP. Weekly lab monitoring was arranged.
